title: Shortest Job Next
statement:
A single processor runs `n` jobs. Job `i` arrives at time `a_i` and needs `d_i` units of time. The processor runs one job at a time and never interrupts a job once it has started.

Whenever the processor becomes free, it looks at the jobs that have already arrived (`a_i` at most the current time) and are not yet done. It starts the one with the smallest `d_i` (if several tie, any of them gives the same total). If no job has arrived, it waits until the next arrival and then decides again.

A job's waiting time is its start time minus its arrival time. Print the total waiting time of all jobs.

## Input
The first line contains `n`. Each of the next `n` lines contains `a_i` and `d_i`. The jobs are not sorted.

## Output
Print the total waiting time.

## Constraints
- `1 <= n <= 8000`
- `0 <= a_i <= 10^9`
- `1 <= d_i <= 10^9`
